newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to privatise 16 firms by end-March.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to privatise 16 firms by end-March.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim cabinet plans to sell 16 major state firms including three cement plants, chemical manufacturer Chimko and Alen Mac cosmetics producer, to raise funds for foreign debt payments, officials said on Wednesday.
"The privatisation procedure for the 16 enterprises has started and we hope to conclude the deals by the end of March," Privatisation Agency director Vesselin Blagoev told reporters.
Speaking after a meeting of a structural reform council set up by the interim cabinet, he said a further 10 enterprises would be sold in April. He gave no further details.
The Pirdop-based copper smelter, which involves concessions on adjacent rail links, is also expected to be sold in March.
The three cement plants, Beloizvorski Cement, Granitoid and Zlatna Panega, will be sold with concessions on the quarries near them, said the council's secretary Mladen Georgiev.
The caretaker government plans to lift restrictions on using debt instruments as means of payment, Georgiev said.

So far buyers have been allowed to pay up to 50 percent of the price in Brady bonds issued to restructure Bulgaria's commercial foreign debt and in Zuncs, issued to compensate domestic bad debts accumulated until 1991.
Earlier this month interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski said the government would also offer a stake in Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim.
The World Bank urged the caretaker cabinet to speed sell-offs of attractive businesses in a bid to rekindle foreign investors' interest in Bulgaria.
The small Balkan country relies on external funding and privatisation proceeds to pay $1 billion in foreign debt payments due this year, one third of which falls in the first quarter.
The caretaker government was appointed three weeks ago after the president disbanded parliament and set early general elections.
